mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP deflator rises by more than 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 3% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months by >3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rising commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS (consumer savings) signals monetary easing accompanied by reduced household liquidity buffers, which initially boosts risk appetite but ultimately leads to negative S&P 500 returns over a 5-day horizon as uncertainty rises.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls AND RSAFS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (payroll employment) above their respective 6-month averages signals a synchronized expansion in housing demand and labor market strength, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-mo avg AND PAYEMS > 6-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a housing supply bottleneck.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for four consecutive months, coupled with stable FEDFUNDS, indicates embedded inflation without policy tightening, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS stable (change < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for six consecutive months, regardless of GDP growth, signals structural labor market weakness that depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid technological adoption that boost productivity.
